correctness.rationale: The proof shows that two initially white universal vertices permanently block every first force. A set of at most s vertices cannot start forcing: with all s universal vertices initially blue, at least four path vertices are white; with s-1 universal vertices, any initial path vertex still sees the uncolored universal and a white path neighbor. The two s+1-vertex cases are exhausted, leading to exactly 2s+2 explicit minimum sets. Symmetric-difference-two checks give precisely the two K_(s+1) blocks and single bridge. These arguments hold for every integer s>=2,n>=4. An independent implementation checks 261879 initial sets and 1062 candidate reconfiguration edges across 54 small instances; finite checks corroborate but do not establish the universal result.

value.rationale: The natural clique-path join family realizes every equal-sized two-clique barbell with clique size at least three as an ordinary zero-forcing token-jumping graph. The exact construction isolates a single reconfiguration bottleneck between arbitrarily large complete blocks while input path length varies freely, and fully classifies all minimum sets; this advances the structural graph-realizability problem beyond scalar forcing numbers or ordinary zero-forcing-set counts.
